title: Oracle phases — a plan declares the phase that writes the tests and the phase that discharges them, and a configured `oracles` provider judges both gates

ground.note: The 2026-09-28 design. It was reopened to Draft and abandoned on 2026-10-20, and this spec re-authors it. Its problem, product goal, terminology and most requirements still hold. What changes: its provider answered the old `{ diagnostics }` document with no `$schema`, it refused a missing provider with exit 2, and its only provider was steme's unbuilt `steme oracles`. Its §9b holds five lifted verdicts: Q1 oracle-side-line, Q2 one-designated, Q3 error-and-refuse, Q4 new-oracle-surface and Q5 explicit-subset.

The gate runner. Steps run in profile order and stop at the first failure or refusal. An `input: "gate-request"` step gets the gate request on stdin, which is saved as `checks-attempt-NN.request.json`. An `output: "gate-report"` step is judged by its report: a checked report passes with no finding on exit 0, and any finding fails the step. A checked report with no finding and a non-zero exit, or an unreadable report, fails as a broken step. A `refused` report records `refused`, writes the reason and remedy to the log, and fails with GateStepRefusedError. A readable report is saved as printed as `checks-attempt-NN.report-SS.json`. The steps that ran go to the attempt's step record and to `gate-attribution.json`. Gate steps run with no time cap.

gate-report: `{ $schema, outcome: "checked", findings, review }` or `{ $schema, outcome: "refused", reason, remedy }`. Any other key is refused at any level. A finding is `{ id, rule, location: { file, lines }, message, related, guide }`. Review notes never fail a step and reach only the reviewer.
gate-request: `{ $schema, phase, base, terminal, phases: [{ id, files }] }`. It has exactly five keys. `base` is the commit the gated phase's branch was created from. The last snapshot is 0.20.0.
A step result is `{ command, surface, result }`, with `result` exactly `pass` | `fail` | `refused`. The current shape is the 0.21.0 snapshot, and the history decoders 0.17.0 and 0.20.0 are frozen.

`SurfaceSchema` is the closed literal `local` | `structural` | `product`. One enum serves three uses: configured gate steps (phaxConfig.ts), gate-attribution, and the phase record's `verifiedSurfaces` (runRecord.ts, format phase-record-manifest, current shape 0.17.0).
A surface is verified when at least one of its steps ran and every one of its steps passed. The result feeds the phase record, the final report and the PR body's 'Verified surfaces' line.

A GateStepRefusedError ends the loop: the gate is recorded as rejected, a GateStepRefused event pauses the phase, and there is no fix prompt and no counted attempt. `phax run` prints 'paused: a gate step refused to run' with the reason and remedy, and writes resume-instructions.md.

Exit families: 2 for plan or config validation, 4 for a gate failure (fix attempts exhausted, or a step refused), 11 for a security or preflight refusal (ModelPreflightError, PlanSectionsPreflightError), and 1 for generic failures and lint.

The provider seats `brief`, `planAuditor` and `architecture` are optional `{ command }` blocks, split on whitespace with no shell. They are present in both PhaxConfigSchema and PhaxUserOverlaySchema and decoded with excess properties refused. A gate step is `{ command, surface, firing, output?: log | gate-report, input?: gate-request }`. `getPhaxConfigJsonSchema` and `getPhaxUserOverlayJsonSchema` feed `phax schema upgrade`.

An extracted and persisted phase: id, (title,) model, effort, planMarkdownAnchor, the three planned-file lists, commit. interactive-phases adds `mode` directly after `optionalFilesToEdit`. The current phax-plan snapshot is 0.17.0.

A plan-document phase spreads the extracted fields and ends with `commit, modelReason, model, effort`. assignment-bounds renames `modelReason` to `assignmentReason`, and interactive-phases adds `mode` after `optionalFilesToEdit`. The 0.25.0 snapshot is cut.
LintCheck is structure | files | commands | models | advisory. A finding is `{ severity, check, phase, message }`, and any error exits 1. interactive-phases adds an `interactive` check.

RUN_PREFLIGHT_CHECKS: gate-profile, required-commands, skill-edit-consent, mcp-allow, records-destination, phase-models, phase-sections. `phax run` runs them before it names the run, and executePlan runs them again as the resume re-check. `phase-models` and `phase-sections` refuse with exit 11.
The headless authoring prompt for a plan states, in one bullet, whether an architecture provider is configured. The bullet is absent for a spec.

FORMAT_IDS and SCHEMA_BORN_FORMAT_IDS list every versioned format, including gate-request, gate-report, brief-request, architecture-request and architecture-report. A new provider format joins both lists.
A format's changed shape lives in `next.schema.json` until the cut renames it to the release. A stamp names the release that last changed the format's shape.

Approved. Its §10 records the joint phase-shape session of 2026-10-20: J1 separate keys, with `oracle` its own key; J2 `mode` after `optionalFilesToEdit`, with `assignmentReason`, `model`, `effort` last and `oracle`'s place left to this spec; J4 one shared check per rule family, refusing with exit 11; J5, at the time, oracle-phases with its own lift.

Draft. It adds `mode` (`headless` | `interactive`) and a `**Mode:** interactive` line after the model, effort and Assignment reason lines, and an interactive phase plans no file to create or edit (q-planned-work, review-only). §10 hands this spec the rule against an interactive phase between an oracle phase and its discharging phase, and the question of which commit the discharge judges after a person's correction.
P3: oracle first when the surface is shown, with the oracle files 'read-only for the implementing phase'. A wrong oracle pauses the run and goes back to the spec.
The `files` of the source package. The published launcher `@lbdremy/phax` (npm/package.json) ships only `bin`, `lib` and README.md. phax's own tests run on Vitest (`vitest run`).
phax's own config: the `standard` gate profile (pnpm format … pnpm test … pnpm audit:architecture, then the terminal build and smoke steps), `pnpm install` as setup, and no provider declared.
The oracle-phases entry still says it waits for `steme oracles` and takes its own plan-document lift.

context:
phax runs a plan as chained phases. Each phase gets its own worktree on `<run.branch>--phase-NN`, branched off the previous phase's branch, and is committed once its gate is green. A red gate opens a same-session fix loop.

The gate is the project's gate profile, an ordered list of steps. Each step is `{ command, surface, firing }`. `surface` is exactly `local` | `structural` | `product`, and `firing` is exactly `every-phase` | `terminal`. A step may also carry two optional keys:
- `input: "gate-request"`: the step gets `{ $schema, phase, base, terminal, phases }` on stdin.
- `output: "gate-report"`: phax judges the step by the gate-report it prints. `{ $schema, outcome: "checked", findings, review }` passes with no finding on exit 0. Any finding fails the step and drives the fix prompt. `{ $schema, outcome: "refused", reason, remedy }` stops the phase for the operator with no fix attempt (exit 4, resumable). Anything unreadable fails as a broken step.

Steps run in order and stop at the first failure or refusal. Each step that ran is recorded in `<phase>/gate-attribution.json` as `{ command, surface, result }`, where `result` is exactly `pass` | `fail` | `refused`. A surface whose steps all passed is a verified surface in the phase record, the run summary and the PR body.

phax.json declares providers as `{ "command" }` blocks, split on whitespace with no shell, and merges them across `phax.json`, `~/.phax/config.json` and `phax.local.json`. `brief` and `architecture` speak versioned request and report formats that each carry a required `$schema`. The headless plan authoring prompt says whether an architecture provider is configured.

`phax plans lint` runs the checks structure, files, commands, models and advisory. The run preflight runs a fixed set of checks before `phax run` names a run, and again when `phax resume` re-checks it. Its plan checks refuse with exit 11.

Two specs reshape a phase in this release:
- assignment-bounds (Approved) renames `modelReason` to `assignmentReason`, which stays among the phase's last three keys.
- interactive-phases (Draft) adds `mode` (`headless` | `interactive`) directly after `optionalFilesToEdit`, a `**Mode:** interactive` line, and an `interactive` check that lint and the run preflight share.

The joint session of 2026-10-20 settled three points for this spec. oracle-phases adds its own `oracle` key (J1), placed after `mode` (J2), and its placement rules form one shared check that refuses with exit 11 (J4).

The 2026-09-28 oracle-phases design answered in the old diagnostics document, refused a missing provider with exit 2, and named steme's unbuilt `steme oracles` as its only provider. It was reopened and abandoned on 2026-10-20, to be re-authored here.

phax's own tests run on Vitest. There, `test.fails` and `it.fails` mark a test that must fail: the run passes when the test fails and fails when it passes.
problem:
An oracle-first plan cannot pass phax's gates today. The gate runs the ordinary test command at every phase, so an oracle phase is red by construction:
- its new tests fail because the code does not exist yet;
- old tests edited to state the new behaviour fail too.

Those failing tests, and the tests it deletes on purpose, are what the oracle phase exists to produce. They are the arbitration a reviewer reads like a spec before any code exists. The only way through today is to keep test and code in one phase. That gives up the separation the plan doctrine asks for (phax-decide-plan P3): the agent that writes the code also writes, and can quietly weaken, what judges it.

The implementing phase has the opposite problem. Nothing stops it from 'fixing' a red oracle by editing its assertion, deleting it or turning it into a skip. Read-only oracle files cannot fix this, because making the oracles live needs at least one edit: removing what kept them green while they were red.

phax cannot learn this per test framework. Vitest, pytest and every other runner mark expected failures differently, and phax's contract is to stay framework-agnostic and delegate such judgments to a provider. The 2026-09-28 design did that, but it had two flaws:
- it waited on a single provider that does not exist, so no plan, phax's own included, could ever declare an oracle phase;
- its request and answer carried no `$schema`, against the rule that every provider request and answer is a versioned phax format.

productGoal.statement:
A plan can declare an oracle phase and the later phase that discharges it, wherever an `oracles` provider is configured, whoever wrote that provider.

In the oracle phase, every added or modified test carries its framework's own expected-failure marker. The ordinary test command stays green, and the runner itself turns a vacuous oracle red. In the discharging phase every marker is gone, and removing them is the only change made to the oracle files since the oracle phase's commit.

phax checks none of this itself. At the gate of those two phases it sends the configured provider a versioned oracle request and judges the `gate-report` answer like any report step. A finding drives the fix loop. A wrong oracle exhausts the loop and pauses the run on what is a spec disagreement, not a bug.

Lint and the run's start preflight hold the declarations to one shared check.

The phax repository carries an example Vitest provider that compares syntax trees, and phax's own phax.json declares it. phax's own plans can then be oracle-first, and provider authors have a working reference.
productGoal.guidingRule: phax knows which phase authors the oracles and which phase discharges them; only the provider knows what an oracle is.

terminology.definition: A test that states the behaviour the code must have and judges the phase that implements it. This spec covers tests only; disposition matrices, fixtures and golden files are out of scope.

A test framework's own annotation for a test that must fail: Vitest `test.fails` and `it.fails`, pytest `xfail(strict=True)`. A marked test that fails passes the run, and a marked test that passes fails it. phax never names, detects or parses a marker; only a provider does.

A phase whose plan.md header carries the oracle declaration. Every test it adds or modifies in its oracle files carries an expected-failure marker, and it may delete tests. It is always a headless phase.

The one later phase that makes an oracle phase's oracles live: it removes every marker and makes the implementation satisfy the oracles. It is the next phase unless the declaration names another. Its own `oracle` is null; its role is derived from the oracle phase's declaration.
An oracle phase together with its discharging phase.

The files an oracle phase lists on its `**Oracle files:**` line: a subset of its planned files to create and to edit. Only these files are sent to the provider and guarded between the pair. The oracle phase's other planned files, such as stubs the tests compile against, are ordinary files.
The commit the oracle phase's branch was created from: the previous phase's commit, or the run's start commit for phase-01.
The commit the oracle phase produced: the tip of its phase branch.

A change to the oracle files, from the oracle commit to the discharging phase's worktree, that only removes expected-failure markers. No assertion changes, no test is deleted, and no skip or todo takes a marker's place. The provider proves this; phax does not.
The command configured as `oracles.command` in any config layer. It answers an oracle request with a `gate-report`.
The `oracle-request` document phax writes on the oracles provider's stdin: `$schema`, `verdict`, `phase`, `oraclePhase`, `base`, `files`, and, on a `discharged` request only, `oracleCommit`.

What an oracle request asks the provider to judge: exactly `authored` (at the oracle phase's gate) or `discharged` (at the discharging phase's gate). The key is named `verdict`, not `mode`, because a phase already uses `mode` for `headless` | `interactive`.

The gate step phax itself appends, after every configured step the attempt fires, at the gate of an oracle phase or a discharging phase. It runs the oracles provider and is recorded under the `oracle` surface.
The one domain check behind lint's `oracles` findings and the run preflight's oracle refusal.
Repository tooling in the phax repository: an oracles provider for Vitest that judges oracle files by their syntax trees. phax's own phax.json declares it, and no phax command runs it.

requirements.title: Declaring an oracle phase in plan.md
requirements.statement: The system shall read a phase of plan.md as an oracle phase when its header paragraph carries an `**Oracle phase:**` line valued `yes` or `discharged by phase-NN` and an `**Oracle files:**` line listing its oracle files. It shall take `yes` to designate the next phase in plan order as the discharging phase.

requirements.title: The oracle key in phax-plan.json and the plan document
requirements.statement: WHEN phax extracts a plan.md or decodes a plan document THE system SHALL carry a required `oracle` key, placed directly after `mode`, on every phase of `phax-plan.json` and of the plan document. On an oracle phase the key is `{ "dischargedBy": "<phase id>", "files": [...] }`, with the discharging phase resolved and the oracle files in declaration order. On every other phase it is `null`.

requirements.title: Rendering the declaration
requirements.statement: WHEN phax renders a plan document to plan.md THE system SHALL write the `**Oracle phase:** discharged by <dischargedBy>` and `**Oracle files:**` lines on each phase whose `oracle` is not null, after that phase's Recommended model, Recommended effort, Assignment reason and Mode lines, and SHALL write no oracle line on any other phase.

requirements.title: Lifted sidecars carry no oracle
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact migrate-documents` lifts a live plan sidecar stamped below the plan-document shape that carries `oracle` THE system SHALL give every lifted phase `oracle: null` and add no oracle line to its plan.md.

requirements.title: Lint: well-formed declaration lines
requirements.statement: IF a phase carries an `**Oracle phase:**` line without an `**Oracle files:**` line or the reverse, an `**Oracle phase:**` value other than `yes` or `discharged by phase-NN`, or either line outside its header paragraph, THEN `phax plans lint` SHALL report an error on the `oracles` check naming the phase and the line.

requirements.title: Lint: a discharging phase that exists and comes after
requirements.statement: IF an oracle phase's discharging phase is absent from the plan or does not come after the oracle phase THEN `phax plans lint` SHALL report an error on the `oracles` check naming the oracle phase and the discharging phase it resolved to.

requirements.title: Lint: one role per phase, one-to-one pairs
requirements.statement: IF a phase is both an oracle phase and a discharging phase, or is the discharging phase of more than one oracle phase, THEN `phax plans lint` SHALL report an error on the `oracles` check naming that phase.

requirements.title: Lint: an oracle phase lists oracle files
requirements.statement: IF an oracle phase's `**Oracle files:**` line lists no file THEN `phax plans lint` SHALL report an error on the `oracles` check naming that phase.

requirements.title: Lint: oracle files are planned by the oracle phase
requirements.statement: IF an oracle phase lists an oracle file that is not among its own planned files to create or to edit THEN `phax plans lint` SHALL report an error on the `oracles` check naming the phase and the file.

requirements.title: Lint: no oracle file planned between the pair
requirements.statement: IF a phase strictly between an oracle phase and its discharging phase names one of that pair's oracle files in its planned files to create, to edit or optionally edit THEN `phax plans lint` SHALL report an error on the `oracles` check naming the intervening phase, the file and the oracle phase.

requirements.title: Lint: no interactive phase between the pair
requirements.statement: IF an interactive phase sits strictly between an oracle phase and its discharging phase THEN `phax plans lint` SHALL report an error on the `oracles` check naming the interactive phase and the oracle pair.

requirements.title: Lint: an interactive phase takes no oracle role
requirements.statement: IF an interactive phase is an oracle phase or a discharging phase THEN `phax plans lint` SHALL report an error on the `oracles` check naming that phase.

requirements.title: Lint: an oracle phase needs a provider
requirements.statement: IF a plan declares an oracle phase and no configuration layer declares an `oracles` provider THEN `phax plans lint` SHALL report an error on the `oracles` check naming the oracle phase and the missing `oracles` key.

requirements.title: One oracles check
requirements.statement: The system shall compute every `oracles` finding in one domain check that `phax plans lint` and the run preflight both call, so that each error lint reports is exactly an error the run preflight refuses on.

requirements.title: Run and resume refuse an ill-formed declaration
requirements.statement: IF the `oracles` check reports an error when `phax run` or `phax resume` runs its preflight THEN the system SHALL refuse before any phase starts (for `phax run`, before the run is named), print every error of the check, leave an existing run's state unchanged, and exit 11.

requirements.title: The oracles provider block
requirements.statement: The system shall accept an optional `oracles` block holding exactly one non-empty `command` in `phax.json`, `~/.phax/config.json` and `phax.local.json`, merged across the layers as `brief` and `architecture` are, and shall refuse any other key inside the block with exit 2.

requirements.title: Schema upgrade describes the block
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax schema upgrade` runs THE system SHALL write a `phax.schema.json` and a `phax.user.schema.json` that both describe the `oracles` block, with the provider contract summarized in the block's description.

requirements.title: A configured step cannot claim the oracle surface
requirements.statement: IF a configured gate step declares the `oracle` surface THEN loading the configuration SHALL fail with exit 2 naming the step's surface, because a configured step's surface stays exactly `local`, `structural` or `product`.

requirements.title: The oracle step at the oracle phase
requirements.statement: WHEN a gate attempt of an oracle phase has run every configured step it fires and all of them passed THE system SHALL run the oracle step, with an `authored` oracle request, as the attempt's last step.

requirements.title: The oracle step at the discharging phase
requirements.statement: WHEN a gate attempt of a discharging phase has run every configured step it fires and all of them passed THE system SHALL run the oracle step, with a `discharged` oracle request, as the attempt's last step.

requirements.title: No oracle step anywhere else
requirements.statement: The system shall run the oracles provider only at the gate of an oracle phase or a discharging phase, and never from `phax plans lint`, `phax validate`, the run preflight, plan authoring or the gate of any other phase.

requirements.title: The oracle request
requirements.statement: The system shall write on the oracle step's stdin an `oracle-request` document with a required `$schema` and exactly the keys of its verdict, and shall save that document beside the attempt's log. The keys are `verdict`, `phase`, `oraclePhase`, `base` (the oracle phase's full base commit), `files` (the oracle files) and, on a `discharged` request only, `oracleCommit` (full).

requirements.title: The spawn contract
requirements.statement: The system shall run the oracle step in the gated phase's worktree as it stands before the phase commit, with the `oracles.command` string split on whitespace and no shell.

requirements.title: The step is judged as a report step
requirements.statement: The system shall judge the oracle step by its stdout and exit code exactly as it judges an `output: "gate-report"` step: a `checked` report with no finding passes on exit 0, any finding fails the step whatever the exit code, and the report is saved as printed beside the attempt's log.

requirements.title: Findings drive the fix loop
requirements.statement: WHEN the oracle step fails with findings THE system SHALL put the findings in the phase's fix prompt, as for any report step, and SHALL run the oracle step again on the next attempt once the configured steps pass.

requirements.title: A refusal pauses the phase
requirements.statement: WHEN the oracles provider answers with a `refused` gate report THE system SHALL record the step as `refused`, make no fix attempt, print the provider's reason and remedy, and pause the run at that phase with exit 4, as for any refused report step.

requirements.title: Provider errors fail the step
requirements.statement: IF the oracles provider cannot be spawned, outruns its time cap, prints no readable gate report, or exits non-zero with no finding THEN the system SHALL fail the oracle step as a broken step and name the reason in the attempt's log.

requirements.title: An undischargeable oracle pauses the run
requirements.statement: WHEN an oracle phase or a discharging phase exhausts its fix loop on a failing oracle step THE system SHALL stop the run as a gate failure with exit 4, resumable at that phase.

requirements.title: Attribution of the oracle step
requirements.statement: WHEN the oracle step runs THE system SHALL record it as the last step of the attempt's step record and of the phase's `gate-attribution.json`, with the `oracles.command` string as its command, `oracle` as its surface, and `pass`, `fail` or `refused` as its result.

requirements.title: The oracle surface is carried like any other
requirements.statement: The system shall count the `oracle` surface among a phase's verified surfaces in the phase record, the run summary and the PR body, by the same rule as every other surface.

requirements.title: Oracle pairs in the review handoff
requirements.statement: The system shall list every oracle pair in the run's `review-handoff.md`, with its oracle phase, its discharging phase and the result of each side's last oracle step, and shall write no such list for a plan with no oracle phase.

requirements.title: Oracle role in the records
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax records explain` resolves the commit of an oracle phase or a discharging phase THE system SHALL name the phase's oracle role, its counterpart phase and its last oracle-step result.

requirements.title: The agent is told its role
requirements.statement: The system shall state in the prompt of an oracle phase and of a discharging phase the phase's oracle role, its counterpart phase and the oracle files, in a fixed wording that names no test framework and no marker.

requirements.title: Discharge edits are planned edits
requirements.statement: WHEN phax reconciles the files a discharging phase touched THE system SHALL count an edit to one of its pair's oracle files as a planned edit.

requirements.title: The discharge judges the current oracle commit
requirements.statement: WHEN a discharging phase's gate runs after a resume, a reset or a re-run THE system SHALL name in the `discharged` request the oracle phase's current commit and its current base commit.

requirements.title: Reset the discharge before its oracles
requirements.statement: IF `phax reset-phase` targets an oracle phase whose discharging phase is no longer pending THEN it SHALL refuse, naming the discharging phase to reset first, and change nothing.

requirements.title: The planner is told a provider is configured
requirements.statement: WHERE an `oracles` provider is configured THE system SHALL state in the headless plan authoring prompt that one is configured and that the planner may declare oracle phases.

requirements.title: The planner is told no provider is configured
requirements.statement: WHERE no `oracles` provider is configured THE system SHALL state in the headless plan authoring prompt that none is configured and that the planner declares no oracle phase.

requirements.title: The planning skill states the rule
requirements.statement: The phax-planning skill shall state that a plan declares an oracle phase only when an `oracles` provider is configured. It shall give the two declaration lines, the oracle files as a subset of the oracle phase's planned files, and the one change the discharging phase may make to those files.

requirements.title: Nothing changes without an oracle phase
requirements.statement: WHILE a plan declares no oracle phase THE system SHALL extract, lint, run, resume, reset and record it with the same findings, prompts, gate steps, attribution and exit codes as before this change, apart from `oracle: null` on every phase, whether or not an `oracles` provider is configured.

requirements.title: No test-framework knowledge in phax
requirements.statement: The system shall neither read the content of an oracle file nor add, remove, reorder or alter a configured gate step in order to judge an oracle.

requirements.title: The example provider is repository tooling
requirements.statement: The phax repository shall carry an example `oracles` provider for Vitest as repository tooling outside the phax CLI, run by no phax command and imported by no phax module.

requirements.title: phax's own config declares the example
requirements.statement: The phax repository's own `phax.json` shall declare the example as its `oracles` provider.

requirements.title: The example judges authored oracles
requirements.statement: WHEN the example provider receives an `authored` request THE example SHALL answer with a `checked` gate report that holds one finding for each test, added or modified since `base` in the oracle files, that does not carry `.fails`, and no finding for a test deleted since `base`.

requirements.title: The example finds markers left at discharge
requirements.statement: WHEN the example provider receives a `discharged` request THE example SHALL report one finding for each `.fails` marker left in the oracle files.

requirements.title: The example proves marker removal is the only change
requirements.statement: WHEN the example provider receives a `discharged` request THE example SHALL report one finding for each oracle file whose syntax tree now differs from its syntax tree at `oracleCommit` with every `.fails` member access removed.

requirements.title: The example compares syntax trees, not lines
requirements.statement: The example provider shall judge oracle files by their syntax trees and never by their lines, so that a change of whitespace, line breaks or trailing commas alone never changes its answer.

requirements.title: The example refuses a request it cannot read
requirements.statement: IF the example provider receives a request it cannot read THEN it SHALL answer with a `refused` gate report naming the reason and a remedy.

## phase-02 — Refund oracles  {#phase-02-refund-oracles}

**Recommended model:** claude-sonnet-5-5
**Recommended effort:** medium
**Oracle phase:** yes
**Oracle files:** tests/refunds.test.ts, tests/prune.test.ts

# or, naming the discharging phase:
**Oracle phase:** discharged by phase-04
**Oracle files:** tests/refunds.test.ts, tests/prune.test.ts

Normative:
- the two lines sit only on an oracle phase, in its header paragraph;
- they come after the Recommended model and Recommended effort lines, and after the Assignment reason and Mode lines when the phase has them (an oracle phase is headless, so in practice it has no Mode line);
- `yes` means the next phase in plan order, and a rendered plan always names the phase;
- the oracle files are a subset of the phase's planned files to create and to edit (Q5), so the phase may also plan a stub such as src/refunds/index.ts that is not an oracle.

## Oracle phases

- Declare an oracle phase only when an `oracles` provider is configured: the authoring prompt says so, and by hand you check `oracles` in phax.json and its overlays. Without one, keep tests and code in one phase.
- The oracle phase writes the tests. Every test it adds or modifies carries the runner's expected-failure marker. It may delete tests, and it may plan stubs the tests compile against; only the files on its `**Oracle files:**` line are oracles.
- Its discharging phase (the next phase, or the one named) removes the markers and writes the code. Removing the markers is the only change it makes to the oracle files.
- No phase in between plans an oracle file, and no interactive phase sits in between.

acceptanceCriteria.name: Plans without oracle phases are unchanged
acceptanceCriteria.given: a plan with no oracle declaration, run once with an `oracles` provider configured and once without
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax plans lint`, `phax run` and `phax records explain` run
acceptanceCriteria.then: both runs produce the same lint findings, prompts, `gate-attribution.json` steps and exit codes, with `"oracle": null` on every phase, no `oracle`-surface step, and the provider never spawned.

acceptanceCriteria.name: phax neither reads oracles nor rewrites the gate
acceptanceCriteria.given: an oracle pair run with a filesystem port that records every read, and a gate profile of three steps
acceptanceCriteria.then: phax itself reads no oracle file path, and each phase's attribution lists the three configured steps unchanged and in order, followed only by the oracle step.

acceptanceCriteria.name: The example stays outside the CLI
acceptanceCriteria.given: the phax repository, its built CLI and its packed npm packages
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax --usage` is read, `src/` is searched for imports, and the packages' file lists are read
acceptanceCriteria.then: no phax command names or runs the example, no module under `src/` imports it, and, under q-example-ships' recommendation, neither npm package contains it.

acceptanceCriteria.name: phax's own config declares the example
acceptanceCriteria.given: the phax repository's phax.json
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax validate` runs and the resolved `oracles.command` is executed on a made-up `authored` request
acceptanceCriteria.then: validation passes, and the command prints a gate-report carrying `$schema`.

acceptanceCriteria.name: The example judges authored oracles
acceptanceCriteria.given: a git repository whose `base` commit holds tests/prune.test.ts with the tests `keeps the newest run` and `drops archived runs`, and a working tree that adds `test.fails('refunds a partial capture', …)` and `it('caps a refund at the invoice total', …)`, modifies `keeps the newest run` without `.fails`, and deletes `drops archived runs`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the example receives an `authored` request for tests/prune.test.ts
acceptanceCriteria.then: it prints a `checked` gate report with exactly two findings, naming `caps a refund at the invoice total` and `keeps the newest run`, and none for the deleted test or the `test.fails` one.

acceptanceCriteria.name: The example finds a marker left at discharge
acceptanceCriteria.given: an oracle commit whose tests/refunds.test.ts holds two `test.fails` tests, and a working tree that removes one of the two markers and changes nothing else
acceptanceCriteria.then: it reports exactly one finding, naming the remaining `.fails`; with both markers removed and nothing else changed, it prints a `checked` report with no finding and exits 0.

acceptanceCriteria.name: The example refuses any other change at discharge
acceptanceCriteria.given: the same oracle commit and, in turn, working trees that remove both markers and also change `toBe(120)` to `toBe(100)`, delete a test, or replace a `test.fails` with `test.skip`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the example receives a `discharged` request for each
acceptanceCriteria.then: each answer holds a finding naming tests/refunds.test.ts.

acceptanceCriteria.name: Reformatting never changes the example's answer
acceptanceCriteria.given: the same oracle commit and a working tree that removes both markers and also re-indents the file, moves its line breaks and adds trailing commas, and separately a `base` and working tree that differ in one unchanged test only by re-indentation
acceptanceCriteria.when: the example receives a `discharged` request for the first and an `authored` request for the second
acceptanceCriteria.then: neither answer holds a finding.

acceptanceCriteria.name: The example refuses a request it cannot read
acceptanceCriteria.given: in turn, a request with no `$schema`, and one whose `verdict` is `approved`
acceptanceCriteria.then: it prints a `refused` gate report carrying `$schema`, a reason naming the defect, and a remedy.

openQuestions.question: Which request does phax write on the oracle step's stdin: a new `oracle-request` format, or the existing `gate-request` extended?

options.label: A new versioned `oracle-request` format: `$schema`, `verdict` (`authored` | `discharged`), `phase`, `oraclePhase`, `base`, `files`, and `oracleCommit` on `discharged` only — two variants, each with exactly its keys
options.abandons: One request reader for every provider phax spawns at a gate. A provider that is both an oracles provider and a configured gate-report step reads two formats, and phax versions, snapshots and publishes one more format.

options.label: The existing `gate-request` gains a required `oracle` key: null for configured steps, and `{ verdict, oraclePhase, oracleBase, oracleCommit, files }` for the oracle step
options.abandons: gate-request's single meaning and its stable shape. Every declaring step's request changes shape for a key only one step reads. Its `base` (the gated phase's) is not the oracle base the verdict needs, so the block repeats a second base. A nullable block also admits combinations, such as a discharged verdict with no oracle commit, that two explicit variants exclude.

openQuestions.rationale: The lost shared reader costs little. phax already gives each provider its own request format (brief-request, architecture-request), and a provider that is also a configured report step is the rare case. Extending gate-request would change a published shape (0.20.0) for every report step in every repository, to carry a block one step reads, and would need a second `base` beside the gated phase's. A separate format keeps both shapes explicit per variant, with no null-filled keys.

openQuestions.question: Where does the example Vitest provider ship?

options.label: Repository tooling only: it lives in the phax repository under `examples/` (or `scripts/`), phax's own plans use it, and it ships in neither npm package
options.abandons: A ready-to-install Vitest provider for other repositories: they copy the example's folder, or write their own against its README.

options.label: Shipped in `@lbdremy/phax` as a second executable beside `phax`
options.abandons: The launcher's thinness and phax's framework neutrality. Every install carries tree-sitter and a TypeScript grammar for one test framework, under phax's own name, and the example's behaviour becomes something each release must keep working.

options.label: Published as its own npm package, released in lockstep with phax
options.abandons: A release with two packages. A third package means another trusted publisher, version check, smoke test and approval in the release workflow, for a tool with one known consumer.

openQuestions.rationale: The operator decided the example is repository tooling, there so that phax's own plans can be oracle-first and provider authors have a reference. Shipping it under phax's name would contradict the guiding rule that only the provider knows what an oracle is. A separate package can be cut later, at no cost to this spec, if a second consumer appears.

openQuestions.question: May an interactive phase be the discharging phase of an oracle phase? (It can never be an oracle phase: oracle files must be planned files to create or edit, and an interactive phase plans none.)

options.label: No: an interactive phase takes no oracle role. It is a lint error and an exit-11 preflight refusal on the `oracles` check
options.abandons: A person writing the implementation against oracles an agent wrote, during the stop, with the oracles provider judging the closing gate.

options.label: Yes: an interactive phase may discharge, and its closing gate runs the oracle step with a `discharged` request
options.abandons: interactive-phases' review-only rule (q-planned-work). Discharging is implementation the planner foresaw, so the phase would carry planned work. A red oracle verdict at closing would also return the phase to the person with no fix loop.

openQuestions.rationale: Discharge is foreseeable work, and interactive-phases decided that foreseeable work belongs to an agent phase under the gate and the fix loop. Refusing also keeps every oracle verdict on a headless phase, where a finding has a fix loop to drive. A person who wants to review the oracles places an interactive phase before the oracle phase, or after the discharge.

settled: Q4's widened surface changes two published shapes: gate-attribution (current shape 0.21.0) and phase-record-manifest (current shape 0.17.0, through `verifiedSurfaces`). Each gets a `next` snapshot and a frozen decoder for its current shape, and documents stamped earlier stay readable. A configured gate step keeps its own three-value enum, so phax.json's JSON Schema still offers only `local`, `structural` and `product`, and `"surface": "oracle"` on a configured step is refused at decode. gate-request and gate-report are unchanged.

The rule against an interactive phase inside a pair settles the question interactive-phases handed over. No person's correction can land between the two phases, so the discharge always judges the oracle phase's own commit. A correction after the discharge belongs to an ordinary interactive phase and runs no oracle step.
`phax validate --plan` stays a decode of `phax-plan.json`. It refuses a phase whose `oracle` is missing or malformed, and runs neither the `oracles` check nor the provider.

Release, under J5 as revised on 2026-10-20, in two cases:
- If this spec is approved before the joint plan-document plan of assignment-bounds and interactive-phases is cut, `oracle` rides that change. There is one frozen copy of the 0.25.0 plan-document shape and one `phax artifact migrate-documents` lift, which renames `modelReason`, writes `mode: "headless"` and writes `oracle: null`. There is one new phax-plan shape carrying `mode` and `oracle`, with a frozen copy of 0.17.0, one treatment of the extraction cache and of in-flight runs, and one upgrading entry. The J5 lines in those two specs and in NEXT_STEPS.md then describe a superseded plan.
- Otherwise this spec takes its own lift after theirs: a frozen copy of the plan-document and phax-plan shapes they cut, a second lift that writes `oracle: null`, its own extraction-cache treatment and its own upgrading entry.
Either way, `oracle-request`, gate-attribution and phase-record-manifest are this spec's own shape changes.
open: The spelling of the plan.md lines, the lint, preflight and refusal messages, the prompt paragraphs, the handoff table, the records-explain line and the skill text. All are indicative.
The provider time cap. 120 s is indicative: it covers a syntax-tree comparison of a few files without letting a hung provider stall an unattended phase. Configured report steps have no cap today.

Where the `oracles` check sits in RUN_PREFLIGHT_CHECKS (after `phase-sections`, beside the `interactive` check), and whether `phax run --dry-run`, which returns before the preflight, reports its errors as a "Preflight will fail" line.

How the oracle role reaches `phax records explain`. Either a new per-phase record field (required, null for ordinary phases, under the no-shims rule), or a derivation from the recorded `phax-plan.json`.

How the example identifies a test across two trees (its `describe` path and title), how it treats `test.each` tables and nested `describe` blocks, whether a comment change counts as a change, and what it answers for an oracle file missing at a commit.
The example's folder (`examples/` or `scripts/`), its command in phax.json, and its parser. web-tree-sitter with the TypeScript grammar as WebAssembly is suggested.
The oracle request's saved file name. `checks-attempt-NN.oracle-request.json` is indicative.
constraints: No back-compat shims. `oracle` is required on every phase of `phax-plan.json` and of the plan document, and is null on every phase that is not an oracle phase. Older sidecars are lifted, never read with the key missing. The plan must say how extraction-cache entries and in-flight runs written by an older binary are treated.
Every provider request and answer carries a required `$schema`. `oracle-request` is born with it and joins FORMAT_IDS and SCHEMA_BORN_FORMAT_IDS.

phax gains no test-framework knowledge: no built-in provider, no marker list and no test-file convention in `src/`. The example lives outside `src/`, so the port rules do not bind it, and nothing in `src/` imports it. It must install without native builds.

Fixtures and examples are made up: acme-billing, refunds, tests/prune.test.ts, tests/refunds.test.ts. Tests hold across a release cut: they assert `$schema` URLs by format id and release pattern, never by the running version.
headless-review is unchanged: its `--append` keeps no oracle-file refusal.

docsPage.page: README §Oracle provider (under §Configure, beside the other providers) and the docs-site page built from it, plus an oracle-phase section in the phax-planning skill
docsPage.reader: Two readers. First, a project owner who wants an agent's tests written before, and judged apart from, the code that satisfies them, and who configures an `oracles` provider: their own, or one adapted from phax's Vitest example. Second, a planner writing an oracle-first plan.
docsPage.example:
In acme-billing's phax.json: "oracles": { "command": "node tools/vitest-oracles.mjs" }.

In plan.md, phase-02 carries `**Oracle phase:** yes` and `**Oracle files:** tests/refunds.test.ts`, and writes `test.fails('caps a refund at the invoice total', …)`. At phase-02's gate, phax sends {"$schema": "…/oracle-request/<release>.json", "verdict": "authored", "phase": "phase-02", "oraclePhase": "phase-02", "base": "3f2a91c…", "files": ["tests/refunds.test.ts"]}, and the provider answers a checked gate report with no finding.

phase-03 removes `.fails` and writes the refund cap. Its gate sends verdict "discharged", with phase-02's commit as oracleCommit. Had phase-03 changed toBe(120) to toBe(100), the provider's finding would drive the fix loop, and an oracle that cannot pass unchanged pauses the run with exit 4.

Without an oracles block, `phax plans lint` reports an error on the oracles check, and `phax run` refuses with exit 11.
